environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 7.0 application deployed behind Azure Front Door Premium with custom WAF policy. PgBouncer 1.21 configured with prepared_statements=named and track_extra_parameters=yes. The PostgreSQL 15 instance has row-level security (RLS) enabled on the users table with a policy that restricts UPDATE operations: the policy function checks that the columns being modified are within an allowed set (username, email, password_hash) by comparing OLD and NEW row values. The RLS policy is: CREATE POLICY user_self_update ON users FOR UPDATE USING (true) WITH CHECK (role = OLD.role AND is_active = OLD.is_active AND account_balance = OLD.account_balance AND mfa_enabled = OLD.mfa_enabled AND mfa_secret IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.mfa_secret AND failed_login_attempts = OLD.failed_login_attempts). The database role used by the application (app_service_user) is not a superuser and has RLS enforced (ALTER TABLE users FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY). PgBouncer query parameterization ensures all EF Core queries go through as parameterized prepared statements, preventing any raw SQL bypass of RLS.

config.rls_policy: CREATE POLICY user_self_update ON users FOR UPDATE USING (true) WITH CHECK (role = OLD.role AND is_active = OLD.is_active AND account_balance = OLD.account_balance AND mfa_enabled = OLD.mfa_enabled AND mfa_secret IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.mfa_secret AND failed_login_attempts = OLD.failed_login_attempts)
